text:
maya: Heads up — SCIM provisioning for Acme started failing right after the KMS alias rotate. Lots of accounts in `pending_deprovision` and the IdP logs show SAML assertions with audience mismatch. Anyone seen this pattern? :eyes:

sanjay: I can look. Can you paste a log snippet and the provisioning config?

henry: saw something similar once — usually encryption-context or aud claim got swapped. But paste logs pls.

maya: log: ```2026-03-21T14:02:12Z WARN scim-provisioner: deprov loop user=acct-123 status=pending_deprovision error="audience mismatch: expected=https://acme.example.com/acs got=https://redwood.internal/" ctx=kms-alias/rot-2026-03```

ops-bot: [deploy-notify] KMS alias rotation completed by @infra-team at 2026-03-21T13:58:01Z :white_check_mark:

lina: Two quick thoughts — (1) RBAC change could've flipped which SP the svc account uses (different client_id -> aud), (2) audit logging should show who used which KMS key for encrypting SCIM payloads. Check CloudTrail/KMS audit.

henry: run `aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://blob.bin --grant-tokens ...`? also check encryptionContext on the ciphertext. If context differs, decryption yields different plaintext that leads to wrong aud mapping.

sanjay: maya, can you dump the scim-provisioner env/config? e.g. client_id, idp_metadata_url, service_account key alias. (redact tokens)

maya: config snippet: ```SCIM_CLIENT_ID=acme-scim-client-01
IDP_METADATA=https://idp.acme.example.com/.well-known/saml-configuration
KMS_ALIAS=alias/redwood-scim/rot-2026-03```

henry: that KMS_ALIAS suffix looks like the new one. If someone rotated and re-wrapped the service key with a different encryption-context (maybe `env=prod` -> `env=staging`), the provisioner might unwrap differently and pick a fallback SP mapping.

sanjay: I'm going to proxy a test authn to see the raw assertion. Give me 5.

deploy-bot: [canary] scim-provisioner v3.2.1 -> v3.2.2 attempted canary at 14:00Z, rolled back to v3.2.1 automatically.

sanjay: found it — the SAML assertion aud is `https://redwood.internal/` because the service-account token was rewrapped with `service=internal-proxy` encryption-context during rotate. CloudTrail shows `kms:ReEncrypt` by infra-rotations@infra-team with ctx {"service":"internal-proxy"}.

lina: oof. So the rotation job used the wrong encryption-context. That causes the provisioner to trust a different client mapping.

maya: confirmed. If we rewrap the key with the previous encryption-context the pending_deprovision clears. Sanjay — can you run re-encrypt with the old context as hotfix?

sanjay: doing it now. `aws kms re-encrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://wrapped.bin --destination-key-id alias/redwood-scim --destination-encryption-context service=acme-scim`

(small pause)

sanjay: hotfix applied, requeued the SCIM jobs, status started moving to active again. users are provisioning. :thumbsup:

henry: follow-ups: 1) add an assertion-level unit test for aud mapping, 2) gating KMS rotates with a small smoke that validates encryption-context, 3) add an alert that watches for mass `pending_deprovision` spikes.

lina: I'll file a post-incident with suggested policy: disallow re-encrypt ops without explicit context tag, and add CloudTrail guardrail to block `ReEncrypt` if `destinationEncryptionContext` != expected.

maya: thanks all — for the incident report I can paste the logs and the CloudTrail event id. Also recommend we add an audit log entry linking KMS alias rotates to the SCIM service-account.

sanjay: one more: add a canary test after any infra key rotate that runs a small SCIM create+delete through the real path (non-prod client) to catch context mismatch.

maya: noted. Marking resolved for now; will open follow-ups in security backlog. :white_check_mark:
